claims.text: Pronounced short-range-order heterogeneities in CrCoNi create local variations in fault energy.
Local fault-energy variations cause intermittent dislocation pinning and jumpy dislocation motion.
Intermittent dislocation pinning caused by SRO heterogeneity increases the measured yield strength.
SRO-induced pinning alters deformation behavior relative to a state with spatially homogeneous SRO.
Controlled processing can produce an intrinsic or enhanced SRO state in CrCoNi.
Thermal homogenization can minimize spatial fluctuations in SRO in CrCoNi.
High-resolution TEM and synchrotron-based diffraction can verify and quantify the proposed difference in SRO distributions.
SRO heterogeneities produce spatial variations in dislocation activation barriers through fluctuations in local shear-fault energies.
The spatially varying activation barriers act as dislocation pinning sites during deformation.
Regions with more pronounced SRO have larger local fault-energy variations.
A homogenized SRO state permits smoother dislocation motion than a heterogeneous SRO state.
A homogenized SRO state has lower yield strength than a heterogeneous SRO state under otherwise identical conditions.
CrCoNi samples with pronounced SRO heterogeneity will exhibit discontinuous, pinned dislocation motion.
CrCoNi samples with pronounced SRO heterogeneity will exhibit higher yield strength than thermally homogenized samples.
The proposed relationship should hold during microcompression from room temperature to approximately 673 K when SRO and other microstructural factors, including grain size, are controlled.
No statistically significant difference in either yield strength or dislocation dynamics between the enhanced-SRO and homogenized-SRO samples would falsify the proposed causal relationship.
